Name: DaybreakDanger
Author: WanderingInsanity
Description:
[heading]Description[/heading]
[b]Daybreak Danger[/b] turns Stardew Valley into a configurable survival challenge. Created by [b]WanderingInsanity[/b], it adds random monster encounters as you explore, adjustable morning stamina, and rare Blood Moon days that make enemies stronger.
Choose which enemies appear, how often they spawn, and whether encounters happen indoors or in Pelican Town. Normal days and Blood Moon days have separate enemy lists, spawn counts, and spawn chances.
Entrance protection and temporary arrival immunity help prevent enemies from trapping you when entering a new area. You can also start a new game with a Rusty Sword and disable overnight health recovery for a tougher experience.

[b]This mod is a work in progress and has had little to no testing! This is the first mod I've made![/b]

[b]This mod was created for my own personal use but I figured someone else may want to try it out.[/b]

[b]Make sure to Edit the Config.json file to your liking (You must launch the game once for it generate the config file)[/b]

[b]I highly recommend you disable health and stamina regen when you sleep to make food matter![/b]

[heading]Installation instructions[/heading]
[spoiler][b]Installing the compiled mod: Install with Vortex OR[/b]
[list=1]
[*]Install Stardew Valley and SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Download and extract the compiled Daybreak Danger mod.[/*]
[*]Place the [b]DaybreakDanger[/b] folder inside your Stardew Valley [b]Mods[/b] folder.[/*]
[*]Make sure
[code]DaybreakDanger.dll[/code]and
[code]manifest.json[/code]are directly inside that folder.[/*]
[*]Launch Stardew Valley through SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Edit
[code]Mods/DaybreakDanger/config.json[/code]to customize the mod.[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]
[heading]Main features[/heading]
[spoiler]Random monster encounters
Each eligible location entry triggers independent spawn rolls. The default is [b]10 rolls with a 20% chance each[/b], producing an average of two potential enemies per visit.
Successful rolls select a random enabled enemy and search for a valid position across the map. Limited space or safety restrictions can reduce the number actually placed.
Walking around within the same location does not trigger another roll. Leaving and returning can trigger more encounters.
[table][tr][th]Setting[/th]
[th]Default[/th]
[th]What it does[/th]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]EnableMonsterSpawns[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Master switch for this mod’s normal and Blood Moon encounters.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]SpawnRollsPerEntry[/code][/td]
[td][code]10[/code][/td]
[td]Normal-day spawn attempts per entry. Range: 0–1000.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]SpawnChancePercent[/code][/td]
[td][code]20[/code][/td]
[td]Independent chance for each normal-day attempt. Range: 0–100%.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]SpawnInTown[/code][/td]
[td][code]false[/code][/td]
[td]Allows encounters on the Pelican Town outdoor map when enabled.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]SpawnIndoors[/code][/td]
[td][code]false[/code][/td]
[td]Allows encounters in interior locations when enabled, including mine maps classified as indoors.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]RollOnDayStart[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Also attempts an encounter in your waking location, subject to location restrictions.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]RollOnReentry[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Allows another roll when returning. When false, each location instance rolls once per day.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]MaxMonstersPerLocation[/code][/td]
[td][code]0[/code][/td]
[td]Limits living monsters present, including native enemies. Zero means unlimited accumulation. Range: 0–10000.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]MinimumDistanceFromPlayers[/code][/td]
[td][code]3[/code][/td]
[td]Minimum spawn distance from players, in tiles. Range: 0–100.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]TileSearchAttemptsPerMonster[/code][/td]
[td][code]200[/code][/td]
[td]Maximum position searches per successful roll. Range: 1–1000.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]ExcludedLocations[/code][/td]
[td][code][][/code][/td]
[td]Internal location names or unique names where this mod should not spawn enemies.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]DebugLogging[/code][/td]
[td][code]false[/code][/td]
[td]Logs encounter results and the daily Blood Moon result to SMAPI.[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]For example,
[code]"ExcludedLocations": ["Farm", "Beach"][/code]prevents this mod’s encounters in those locations.
Town protection covers the outdoor [b]Town[/b] map. Buildings accessed from town are controlled by the indoor setting and location exclusions.
Scripted events and festivals skip encounter rolls. Surviving mod-spawned enemies normally remain when you leave, but are removed at day end before the overnight save. Drops from defeated enemies remain.
Separate normal and Blood Moon enemy lists
The mod supports [b]25 enemy types and variants[/b].
[list]
[*][code]Monsters[/code]controls the normal-day enemy pool.[/*]
[*][code]BloodMoonMonsters[/code]controls the Blood Moon enemy pool.[/*]
[/list]Every entry has its own
[code]true[/code]or
[code]false[/code]switch. All entries default to
[code]true[/code]in both pools.

[list]
[*][b]Slimes:[/b]
[code]GreenSlime[/code],
[code]BlueSlime[/code],
[code]RedSlime[/code],
[code]PurpleSlime[/code][/*]
[*][b]Big Slimes:[/b]
[code]BigGreenSlime[/code],
[code]BigBlueSlime[/code],
[code]BigRedSlime[/code],
[code]BigPurpleSlime[/code][/*]
[*][b]Skeletons:[/b]
[code]Skeleton[/code],
[code]SkeletonMage[/code][/*]
[*][b]Shadow enemies:[/b]
[code]ShadowBrute[/code],
[code]ShadowShaman[/code],
[code]Shooter[/code](Shadow Sniper)[/*]
[*][b]Crabs:[/b]
[code]RockCrab[/code],
[code]LavaCrab[/code],
[code]IridiumCrab[/code],
[code]TruffleCrab[/code][/*]
[*][b]Other enemies:[/b]
[code]DustSprite[/code],
[code]MetalHead[/code],
[code]HotHead[/code],
[code]FalseMagmaCap[/code],
[code]PepperRex[/code],
[code]Leaper[/code](Spider),
[code]Mummy[/code],
[code]DwarvishSentry[/code][/*]
[/list]
Enabled enemies have equal selection weight. Setting every entry in a pool to
[code]false[/code]stops encounters from that pool.
During a Blood Moon, its pool [b]replaces[/b] the normal pool. It does not add another set of rolls on top. You could allow only slimes normally, then enable skeletons, mummies, and Pepper Rex during Blood Moons.
These switches control this mod’s selections; they do not disable native enemy spawns. Enemies retain their usual combat mechanics, disguises, drops, and special attacks.
Blood Moon days
By default, each day has a [b]1% chance[/b] to become a Blood Moon.
A morning message announces the event, a subtle red overlay appears outdoors, and monsters receive [b]double maximum health and base damage[/b] for the day.
The daily result is stable for that save and day, so reloading does not give another chance to reroll it.
[table][tr][th]Setting[/th]
[th]Default[/th]
[th]What it does[/th]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]EnableBloodMoon[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Master switch for Blood Moon events and effects.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonChancePercent[/code][/td]
[td][code]1[/code][/td]
[td]Daily event chance. Range: 0–100%.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]EnableBloodMoonSpawns[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Allows Blood Moon encounter rolls. Disabling it does not fall back to normal-day encounters.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonSpawnRollsPerEntry[/code][/td]
[td][code]10[/code][/td]
[td]Spawn attempts per entry during the event. Range: 0–1000.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonSpawnChancePercent[/code][/td]
[td][code]20[/code][/td]
[td]Chance per event-day attempt. Range: 0–100%.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonMonsters[/code][/td]
[td]All enabled[/td]
[td]Individual enemy switches for Blood Moon encounters.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]EnableBloodMoonAnnouncement[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Shows the morning announcement.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonAnnouncement[/code][/td]
[td]“A Blood Moon rises today! Monsters are stronger. Beware!”[/td]
[td]Custom announcement text.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]EnableBloodMoonTint[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Enables the screen colour overlay.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonTintOutdoorsOnly[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Limits the tint to outdoor locations.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonTintStrengthPercent[/code][/td]
[td][code]12[/code][/td]
[td]Overlay intensity. Range: 0–100%.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonTintRed[/code][/td]
[td][code]255[/code][/td]
[td]Red colour component. Range: 0–255.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonTintGreen[/code][/td]
[td][code]0[/code][/td]
[td]Green colour component. Range: 0–255.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonTintBlue[/code][/td]
[td][code]0[/code][/td]
[td]Blue colour component. Range: 0–255.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]EnableBloodMoonHealthBoost[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Enables enemy health scaling.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonHealthMultiplier[/code][/td]
[td][code]2[/code][/td]
[td]Health multiplier. Range: 0.01–100; 1 means normal health.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]EnableBloodMoonDamageBoost[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Enables enemy base-damage scaling.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonDamageMultiplier[/code][/td]
[td][code]2[/code][/td]
[td]Damage multiplier. Range: 0.01–100; 1 means normal damage.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]BloodMoonAffectsAllMonsters[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Includes native and other-mod enemies. When false, boosts only Daybreak Danger’s tagged monsters.[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]Only the [b]tint[/b] is outdoors-only by default. Monster boosts also apply indoors and in the mines, even where this mod’s encounters are disabled.
Boosts are not multiplied repeatedly. Injured monsters keep their current health percentage when their maximum health changes. Surviving monsters’ normal stats are restored at day end.
Damage scaling changes the enemy’s base damage statistic. Actual hits still follow normal defence, invulnerability, and special-attack rules.
Safer spawning and map entrances
Spawn checks inspect the chosen tile and the monster’s full hitbox, including larger enemies. Wall layers, blocked ground tiles, water, occupied tiles, missing map tiles, and game-reported obstacles are rejected.
Entrance protection also considers known map exits, incoming warp destinations, and actual player landing positions.
[table][tr][th]Setting[/th]
[th]Default[/th]
[th]What it does[/th]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]ProtectMapEntrances[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Keeps new encounters away from known entrance and crossing points.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]EntranceSafeRadiusTiles[/code][/td]
[td][code]6[/code][/td]
[td]Spawn exclusion radius around those points. Range: 0–30 tiles.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]ClearEnemiesNearArrival[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Removes existing enemies near your arrival position.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]ArrivalSafeRadiusTiles[/code][/td]
[td][code]6[/code][/td]
[td]Arrival clearing and spawn-safety radius. Range: 0–30 tiles.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]EnableArrivalImmunity[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Temporarily blocks player damage after entering a location.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]ArrivalImmunitySeconds[/code][/td]
[td][code]2[/code][/td]
[td]Shield duration. Range: 0–60 real-time seconds.[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]Arrival clearing includes native, other-mod, and Daybreak Danger enemies within the configured area. It does not award kills or drops.
Enemies can move toward entrances later; the nearby area is cleared again when you return. The arrival shield also applies when the morning begins. Its timer uses real time, so opening a menu does not extend it.
Morning stamina, starting sword, and sleep healing
[table][tr][th]Setting[/th]
[th]Default[/th]
[th]What it does[/th]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]EnableStartingStamina[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Sets your current stamina each morning.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]StartingStamina[/code][/td]
[td][code]100[/code][/td]
[td]Absolute starting energy points, clamped to your current maximum. Zero is allowed.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]GiveRustySwordOnFirstDay[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Gives a Rusty Sword on Spring 1, year 1, once per player.[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td][code]HealHealthAfterSleep[/code][/td]
[td][code]true[/code][/td]
[td]Allows normal overnight healing. Set false to prevent health recovery from sleeping.[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]The stamina setting changes current energy, not maximum energy or normal tool costs.
The starting sword has a saved per-player marker to prevent repeated gifts. If a Rusty Sword is already in your inventory, another is not added. A full inventory opens the standard item pickup menu.
With overnight healing disabled, sleeping at [b]35 HP[/b] leaves you at no more than [b]35 HP[/b] the next morning. Food, healing items, bathhouse recovery, and other healing systems remain available. This setting is separate from morning stamina.
Multiplayer behaviour
The host’s location entries trigger encounter rolls. Farmhand-only entries do not trigger additional encounters in this version.
The host manages monster boosts and arrival clearing. Blood Moon status is synchronized from the host, while each installed copy provides its player’s visuals, stamina setting, starting sword, and arrival immunity.
Install the same version on every player’s computer. Multiplayer and split-screen integration have not been fully tested.[/spoiler]

[heading]Requirements[/heading]
[spoiler][list]
[*][b]Stardew Valley 1.6 for PC.[/b][/*]
[*][b]SMAPI 4.5.2 or later.[/b][/*]
[*]No Content Patcher or Generic Mod Config Menu requirement.[/*]
[*]Harmony is supplied through SMAPI; no separate Harmony download is required.[/*]
[/list]Settings are edited directly in
[code]config.json[/code][/spoiler]
